column1: You May Experience Reduced Return and Delays on Your Notes Resulting from Changes in the Sponsor’s Servicing System
column3: The Sponsor intends to implement a new servicing system. Although not anticipated, it is possible that the implementation of the new servicing system could result in certain portions of the servicing system not operating as expected, resulting in a loss of functionality or data delays, which could adversely affect the servicing of the Receivables. Further, in anticipation of the implementation of the new system, the Sponsor modified certain system processes as of January 2026 related to the reporting of the Delinquency Threshold Amount, the portion of a scheduled payment that an obligor must fail to pay to be classified as delinquent, from $40 to 10% of the applicable scheduled payment. Although the Sponsor does not currently anticipate that the process modification related to the Delinquency Threshold Amount will have a material adverse effect on the number of contracts determined to be delinquent or defaulted compared to the number that would have been so determined without the change, no assurance can be given that this change will not have a material adverse effect.

column1: The Adverse Events Arising from Pandemics, Epidemics and Other Wide-Spread Public Health Events May Result in Losses or Delays in Payment on Your Notes
column3: Pandemics, epidemics and other  wide-spread public health events, have led, and may in the future lead, to disruptions and volatility in the financial markets and general  economic activity, as businesses and federal, state, and local governments take broad actions intended to mitigate the public health crisis.  The resultant increases in unemployment, decreases in consumer spending and reduced demand for certain products, including abrupt declines  in new and used vehicle sales and downward pressure on used vehicle values, disruptions in global supply chains and shutdowns of manufacturing  capacity in certain industries, including those of auto manufacturers, and decreases in liquidity of certain secondary markets, along  with the various laws, regulations, executive orders, local ordinances and other guidance implemented to combat the effects of a pandemic,  epidemic or wide-spread public health event could have negative effects on the business of World Omni Financial Corp. and on its customers,  dealers, and competitors.  The economic uncertainty resulting  from a pandemic, epidemic or other wide-spread public health event could result in increased delinquencies and defaults by obligors due  to financial hardship or otherwise. In addition, federal, state or local governments may enact laws, regulations, executive orders or  other guidance related to financial obligations such as the Receivables, including allowing obligors to forgo making scheduled payments,  requiring certain modifications or waiving certain fees, or curtailing the ability of creditors to exercise certain rights such as repossessions  and liquidations of financed vehicles. Furthermore, the Servicer may implement a range of actions with respect to affected obligors and  the related Receivables to extend or modify the payment schedule consistent with the Servicer’s customary servicing procedures.  See “World Omni Financial Corp.’s Automobile Finance Business—Servicing” and “Description of the  Trust Documents—Servicing Procedures.” The occurrence of any such events could have an adverse effect on World Omni Financial  Corp.’s ability to operate its business or perform its obligations under the trust
